blogs.title: When CK Won’t Behave: Distinguishing GLP-1–Associated Rhabdomyolysis from Immune-Mediated Necrotising Myopathy
blogs.description: This post would contrast direct toxic muscle injury with autoimmune necrotising myopathy in patients exposed to GLP-1 receptor agonists. It would emphasize how a delayed, progressive course with worsening proximal weakness, bulbar symptoms, persistent CK elevation off drug, and response to steroids/IVIG argues against simple rhabdomyolysis.

blogs.title: Seronegative but Not Benign: Diagnosing IMNM When HMGCR and SRP Are Negative
blogs.description: A practical review of how to diagnose seronegative IMNM when standard myositis antibodies are unrevealing. The post would cover the limitations of antibody panels, the value of MRI for identifying affected muscle, and the biopsy findings that support IMNM, while also discussing how to interpret low-yield serologies such as isolated SS-B positivity.

blogs.title: Bulbar Weakness in Myositis: When Dysphagia and Dysphonia Should Escalate Your Treatment
blogs.description: This piece would focus on dysphagia, dysphonia, and severe proximal weakness as high-risk features of inflammatory myopathy. It would discuss why these findings often justify pulse-dose steroids and early IVIG, how to monitor for aspiration and respiratory decline, and how bulbar involvement changes the urgency of management.

blogs.title: AST, ALT, and the Muscle-Liver Trap: Don’t Miss Myopathy in the Patient with ‘Known Fatty Liver’
blogs.description: This post would use the case to explore how chronic NAFLD can obscure recognition of muscle disease. It would review how to think through aminotransferase elevations in parallel with CK, when transaminitis may be muscle-derived, and why pre-existing liver disease should not derail an evaluation for myositis.

blogs.title: Troponin, BNP, and a Weak Patient: Sorting Cardiac Involvement in Necrotising Myopathy
blogs.description: A clinically oriented discussion of possible cardiac involvement in IMNM, using this patient’s troponin elevation, atrial fibrillation, BNP elevation, and cardiac MRI edema as a springboard. The post would examine how to approach myocarditis versus stress cardiomyopathy versus non-specific biomarker leak in systemic inflammatory illness.

blogs.title: One Dose, Four Months Later: Pharmacovigilance Lessons from a Possible Semaglutide-Triggered Autoimmune Myopathy
blogs.description: This broader post would examine how clinicians should think about rare, serious adverse events linked to increasingly common drugs like semaglutide. It would cover temporal association versus causation, application of WHO-UMC causality criteria, why rechallenge is often unethical, and how case reports should influence counseling and surveillance without overstating certainty.
